ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Liliʻuokalani Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Urgent visit the morning after 20 minutes of right hand weakness and word-finding difficulty: examination, ABCD2 score, ECG and same-day emergency stroke evaluation with CT, CT angiography, swallow screen and antiplatelet loading, with culturally safe care and her ʻohana present at her choice. Concerns: She wants to keep playing and composing, and fears losing the use of her right hand or her words; She wants her ʻohana involved as she chooses, and her own Native Hawaiian ways of healing respected; She wants to be told plainly what is planned and to make her own decisions. [S]

tr.td: Aspirin 81 mg delayed-release oral tablet, one tablet daily for 21 days, after a 325 mg loading dose in the emergency department
Clopidogrel 75 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily, after a 300 mg loading dose in the emergency department
Atorvastatin 40 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Losartan 25 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Apixaban 5 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice daily

tr.td: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram in the clinic: sinus rhythm at 72 per minute, normal intervals, no atrial fibrillation or acute changes
Non-contrast CT of the head in the emergency department: no hemorrhage, no established infarct, mild age-related volume loss

CT angiography of the head and neck: no large-vessel occlusion or intracranial stenosis; calcified plaque at the origin of the left internal carotid artery with less than 50% narrowing; right carotid and vertebral arteries normal
MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging: an 8 mm acute infarct in the cortex of the left precentral gyrus; no hemorrhage; mild white matter changes of small-vessel disease
Transthoracic echocardiography: ejection fraction 60%, mildly enlarged left atrium, no thrombus or valve vegetation, mild mitral annular calcification, no significant valve disease
30-day ambulatory electrocardiographic monitor (adhesive patch with an event recorder), applied at the stroke clinic
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with her consent and with the members of her ʻohana she invited

list.item: Native Hawaiian elder (kupuna), composer, musician and leader of her people; lives at Washington Place, her home of many years, in Honolulu, with members of her household; asked to be called Liliʻuokalani [S]
Speaks Hawaiian and English; chose English for her visits, with Hawaiian words where she prefers them; reads and writes music daily and plays the piano [S]
ʻOhana: she wants members of her ʻohana, including those joined to her by hānai, present when decisions are made, and she makes the decisions; she does not want to be a burden to them [S]
Faith: a lifelong Christian and member of her church; she prays daily; the hospital chaplain was offered and she will ask for her own minister if she wishes [S]

History: she lived through the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom, backed by U.S. forces, imprisonment in her own palace and a forced abdication; she spoke of it briefly and with composure, and said she wants to be told plainly what is planned and to decide for herself [S]

Traditional healing: she has her own Native Hawaiian practices and practitioners and will decide whether and how they are part of her care; lomilomi through a Native Hawaiian Health Care System and hoʻoponopono with her ʻohana were offered alongside clinic care, and nothing further was asked [S]
Diet: fish, poi and kalo, greens, fruit and rice, with some salted fish and preserved foods; never smoked; alcohol rarely, a glass of wine on occasions [S]
Strengths, supports and purpose: her music, her faith, her ʻohana, her work for the welfare of Hawaiian children, and a steadfast, composed manner [S]

tr.td: Urgent visit the morning after 20 minutes of right hand weakness and word-finding difficulty: examination, ABCD2 score, ECG and same-day emergency stroke evaluation with CT, CT angiography, swallow screen and antiplatelet loading, with culturally safe care and her ʻohana present at her choice
Stroke clinic the next morning: diffusion MRI, echocardiogram, 30-day rhythm monitor, cognition screen and vascular neurology consultation
Five-week review: rhythm monitor result, anticoagulation decision, lipids, kidney function and blood pressure
Three-month review after the stroke: function, mood, blood pressure, apixaban safety and falls
Five-month review: blood pressure, lipids, apixaban safety, cognition and plans for the months ahead
Same-day sick visit for a nosebleed on apixaban

Culturally safe, trauma-informed care: address her as Liliʻuokalani, as she asked; take time; explain each test and treatment plainly before it is done; involve her ʻohana as she chooses while she makes the decisions; acknowledge the history of the overthrow when she raises it, without probing

Same-day emergency stroke evaluation today (CT, CT angiography of the head and neck, swallow screen and laboratory tests), then vascular neurology consultation at the rapid-access stroke clinic tomorrow morning, with diffusion MRI and an echocardiogram

Dual antiplatelet therapy started within 24 hours of onset once CT excluded bleeding: aspirin 325 mg and clopidogrel 300 mg loading doses, then aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 21 days, then a single antiplatelet; stop antiplatelets if anticoagulation is started
Atorvastatin 40 mg daily, a high-intensity statin, with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks; LDL goal below 70 mg/dL
Bedside swallow screen before any food or drink, a cognition screen (MoCA) at the stroke clinic, a depression screen, and a falls assessment
BE FAST: balance, eyes, face, arm, speech, time to call 911; call 911 at once for any new symptom, even if it passes, and do not drive herself

Native Hawaiian healing alongside clinic care, if she wishes: lomilomi through Ke Ola Mamo, a Native Hawaiian Health Care System, with the practitioner told that she takes blood thinners, and hoʻoponopono with her ʻohana as they choose; the clinic asks nothing further about her practices

Blood pressure: home readings twice daily for a week; if the average is 130/80 mmHg or higher after the first week, start losartan 25 mg daily, with potassium and creatinine two weeks later; target below 130/80 mmHg

Rhythm monitoring for atrial fibrillation for 30 days with an ambulatory patch, because the stroke is embolic in pattern; if atrial fibrillation is found, stop antiplatelets and start a direct oral anticoagulant

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 6, HAS-BLED 2), with clopidogrel stopped; blood count and kidney function before starting and about every five to six months at her age and kidney function; bleeding precautions, no anti-inflammatory pain medicines, and a falls plan
Laboratory tests drawn at clinic visits, or at home by the clinic's nurse, instead of separate trips to the laboratory
Daily walking, the foods she already eats with less salted and preserved food, alcohol kept to rare occasions, and no smoking
No recurrent stroke or transient ischemic attack
None in five months on dual antiplatelets, then apixaban
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg at home and in the clinic
Anticoagulation that is safe and taken as prescribed, without major bleeding
Apixaban 5 mg twice daily from five weeks; one minor nosebleed, controlled at home and in the clinic; no missed doses
Keep playing the piano and composing
Playing daily; modified Rankin Scale 1 at three months

list.item: Independent in all daily activities; walks without an aid; plays the piano daily; no falls in the past year [S]
Alert, dignified and composed; speech fluent with no word-finding difficulty today; precise in her history; worried about another episode and about her ʻohana; mood steady [S]
